nodes.label: tests workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs the unit/multi-node/smoke suite plus the README-badge updater on any change that could plausibly affect a test result. Concurrency is grouped by github.ref so develop pushes queue (preserving every commit's README state) while PR re-pushes cancel.

nodes.label: test job (typecheck + suite with coverage)
nodes.rationale: One run, one source of truth. The suite used to run twice, which gave the parser a different bun output than the one the build status came from — a flaky test under coverage instrumentation could push the badge to '1489 of 1490' while the build stayed green. Read-only and credential-free because this job installs and executes the entire devDependency tree (#622).

nodes.label: README badges job
nodes.rationale: The only job here that can write to the repository and deliberately the only one that runs no third-party code (#622): it installs nothing, builds nothing and re-runs nothing. Runs on !cancelled() rather than success(), because a red suite is exactly when the badge has to flip to red. Values reach the script through env: rather than ${{ }}, since a workflow expression is pasted into the shell before it runs.

nodes.label: JUnit test-count parser
nodes.rationale: Bun 1.3.14 stopped printing the trailing summary block under GitHub Actions, so the old console scrape matched nothing — and a `[[ -z $PASS ]] && PASS=0` fallback turned 'the parser found nothing' into a plausible zero and pushed a tests-0 of 0 badge from a green run. Now it reads a contract that does not move between bun releases and treats an unreadable count as an error rather than as zero. Output goes to a FILE, never through a pipe: ~8700 annotation lines through a command-substitution pipe made bun die mid-flush with WriteFailed.

nodes.label: Coverage-floor gate step (>= 80%)
nodes.rationale: An unevaluated gate must not read as a passing one, so an unparseable coverage figure fails the step rather than skipping it — unlike the test counts, which only render a badge and must never block a release on a cosmetic parse failure. The 80 floor is pragmatic because the quarantined worker-thread suites remove coverage of machinery that physically cannot execute on a hosted runner.

nodes.label: Frozen-lockfile install policy
nodes.rationale: An unfrozen install resolves whatever package.json's ranges allow right now, so a required check could pass against a dependency set no lockfile ever recorded and nobody could reproduce. Dependabot does not speak the Bun lockfile format, so its PRs fail here until bun.lock is regenerated — that is the intended signal, and #817 is what removes the manual step.
